title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Ionization Energy
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: First Ionization Energy (IE$_1$) is best defined as:
options: Energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom
Energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron from an isolated gaseous atom
Energy required to remove an electron from a solid metal
Energy required to split a molecule into atoms
questions.explain: Ionization energy is specifically defined for an isolated **gaseous** atom losing an electron to form a cation. It is an endothermic process.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which element in Period 2 has a higher First Ionization Energy than expected due to a stable fully-filled $2s$ subshell?
questions.explain: Beryllium ($1s^2 2s^2$) has a stable, full $2s$ subshell. Boron ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^1$) has its outer electron in a $2p$ orbital, which is higher energy and penetrates less than $2s$. Thus, removing an electron from B is easier than from Be, making $IE_{Be} > IE_B$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is the first ionization energy of Oxygen ($O​$) lower than that of Nitrogen ($N​$)?
options: Oxygen has a larger atomic radius
Nitrogen has a stable half-filled $2p$ subshell ($2p^3$)
Oxygen has a higher effective nuclear charge
questions.explain: Nitrogen has a configuration of $2p^3$ (half-filled, stable). Oxygen has $2p^4$; the 4th electron must pair up in one of the p-orbitals, causing electron-electron repulsion that makes it easier to remove compared to the stable unpaired configuration of Nitrogen.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The successive ionization energies (in kJ/mol) for an element are: $IE_1 = 738$, $IE_2 = 1450$, $IE_3 = 7730$, $IE_4 = 10500$. To which group does this element belong?
questions.explain: Notice the massive jump between $IE_2$ (1450) and $IE_3$ (7730). This indicates that the core electrons are being removed after the 2nd electron. Therefore, the element has **2 valence electrons**, placing it in Group 2 ($Mg$ fits these values).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following elements generally has the highest First Ionization Energy in the entire periodic table?
questions.explain: Helium has the smallest atomic radius and a full valence shell ($1s^2$) close to the nucleus without shielding from inner shells. It holds its electrons most tightly.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which factor primarily causes Ionization Energy to decrease down a group?
options: Increasing shielding effect and atomic radius
questions.explain: Down a group, new electron shells are added. The outer electrons are further from the nucleus and are shielded by more inner shells, reducing the effective attraction and making removal easier.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Consider the second ionization energy ($IE_2$). Which element would have an exceptionally high $IE_2$?
questions.explain: Sodium ($Na$) is in Group 1. After losing 1 electron, it achieves the stable configuration of Neon. Removing a **second** electron breaks this stable noble gas core, requiring a tremendous amount of energy.
